'''Kapil Hari Paranjape''' is an Indian [[mathematician]] specializing in [[algebraic geometry]]<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VU8m9ngSNrM |title=RSTV Eureka}}</ref> . He is Professor Emeritus of Mathematics at the [[Indian Institute of Science Education and Research, Mohali]] and Distinguished Professor at the Shiv Nadar Institution of Eminence <ref>{{cite web |url=https://snu.edu.in/faculty/kapil-hari-paranjape/ |title=Shiv Nadar Institution of Eminence}}</ref>

==Biography==
He was born in [[Mumbai]], Maharashtra near the [[Kabootar Khana]] in [[Dadar]] but grew up in [[New Delhi]]. He completed his schooling from the [[Sardar Patel Vidyalaya]] in 1977. He then joined the [[Indian Institute of Technology Kanpur]] where he pursued a five-years integrated Master’s programme in Mathematics and graduated in 1982.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.iitk.ac.in/dora/alumni-profile |title=Notable Alumni of IIT Kanpur}}</ref> He was awarded the General Proficiency Prize for Mathematics from IIT Kanpur in 1982.

He joined the School of Mathematics, [[Tata Institute of Fundamental Research]] and was awarded his PhD in Mathematics in 1992.

Paranjape is also involved in the promotion of [[Linux]] and [[GNU]]<ref>{{cite web|title=Kapil Hari Paranjape|url=http://www.iitk.ac.in/LDP/LDP/LGNET/authors/kapil.html|publisher=Linux Gazette|access-date=29 June 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131227094459/http://www.iitk.ac.in/LDP/LDP/LGNET/authors/kapil.html|archive-date=27 December 2013|url-status=dead}}</ref> and writes a blog titled Mast Kalandar.<ref>{{cite web|title=Mast Kalandar|url=http://www.imsc.res.in/~kapil/blog/|publisher=Linux Gazette|access-date=21 Feb 2014}}</ref>

==Career==
He worked as a Reader at TIFR from 1993-1998. During this time he also held various visiting positions at 
the [[University of Chicago]], [[University of Paris-Sud]] and [[University of Warwick]]. He was appointed as Professor at the Theoretical Statistics and Mathematics Unit of the [[Indian Statistical Institute]], Bangalore. He moved to the [[Institute of Mathematical Sciences, Chennai]] in 1996. Between 2001 and 2009 he held visiting positions at the [[California Institute of Technology]]. Since 2009 he is a professor of Mathematics at the [[Indian Institute of Science Education and Research, Mohali]]. He was Clark Way Harrison Visiting Professor in [[Washington University in St. Louis]] in 2019. He also spent time at the Lodha Mathematical Sciences Institute in 2026. <ref>{{cite web|title=LMSI Interview |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=U4d8aIc8x1Y}}</ref>

==Awards and honors==
He was awarded the [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize for Science and Technology]] in 2005, the highest science award in [[India]],  in the mathematical sciences category. His citation read "Dr Paranjape has made outstanding contributions in the field of algebraic geometry, especially the theory of [[algebraic cycle]]s. He has made highly significant contributions in connecting [[Hodge theory|Hodge Theory]] to the study of [[Chow group|Chow Groups]]. He has also established deep relations between Calabi-Yau varieties and [[modular form]]s".<ref name=INSA>{{cite web|title=Indian Fellow: Kapil Hari Pranjape|url=http://insaindia.org/detail.php?id=P10-1522|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140226040247/http://insaindia.org/detail.php?id=P10-1522|url-status=dead|archive-date=26 February 2014|publisher=[[Indian National Science Academy]]|access-date=29 June 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Awards For Science And Technology 2005|url=http://www.dst.gov.in/awards/award05.htm|publisher=Department of Science & Technology, Govt of India|access-date=29 June 2013|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130914135958/http://www.dst.gov.in/awards/award05.htm|archive-date=14 September 2013}}</ref> He is also a recipient of various other honors, among them are

*Fellowship of [[Indian Academy of Sciences]] Bangalore, 1997
*Fellowship of [[National Academy of Sciences, India|National Academy of Sciences]], Allahabad, 1999
*Associate of the [[International Centre for Theoretical Physics|ICTP]], [[Trieste]], 1999-2001
*[[Brij Mohan Birla|B. M. Birla]] award for young scientists, 1999
*[[Department of Science and Technology (India)|DST]] Swarnajayanti (Golden Anniversary) Grant, 2001
*[[National Board for Higher Mathematics|NBHM]] National Lecturer, India, 2004-2005
*[[Debian]] Developer, 2007
*Fellowship of [[Indian National Science Academy]], New Delhi, 2009
*[[Jagadish Chandra Bose|J C Bose]] National Fellowship, 2010
*Fellowship of [[The World Academy of Sciences]] ([[TWAS]]), 2019
